title: shared-dhcp-scope-bleed-causing-clientside-dns-override
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS resolution to internal hostnames after a VPC peering switchover. Investigation shows that during peering failover we are briefly re-applying a shared DHCP option set (domain-name-servers / domain-search) from the peered control plane to tenant subnets, which causes client systems inside the dedicated tenant to use the wrong recursive resolver and search domains until their DHCP leases renew. This manifests as resolution of private hostnames returning addresses from the wrong tenant or failing altogether. The issue affects Dedicated tenants using shared on-prem/VPC DHCP option profiles when peering state changes occur.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy two Dedicated tenant VPCs with peering via our managed peering controller and configure a shared DHCP options set that contains custom domain-search and DNS resolver entries.
2) Attach tenant instances (simulated customer VMs) and confirm DNS resolution uses tenant resolver and search domains.
3) Trigger a peering failover (simulate control-plane flip by restarting peering agent or forcing route reattachment).
4) Observe DHCP option broadcast/update sequence; verify tenant instances temporarily receive the shared DHCP options pointing to the peered plane's resolvers.
5) Note DNS resolution failures or cross-tenant hostname resolution until client DHCP lease renewal or manual dhclient restart.
impact: High. Several production customers experiencing intermittent outages for internal hostname resolution after peering events. Symptoms include service-to-service failure inside tenant networks, monitoring alert noise, and customer escalations to support/AE teams. The issue increases blast radius during peering maintenance or region failovers.
mitigation: Applied targeted control-plane guard: on peering state transitions we now avoid writing DHCP option overrides to tenant DHCP configurations. A live rollback was deployed for the most recent change that updated the peering reconciliation loop (rollback reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/abcd1234). For affected customers we documented immediate remediation: force DHCP renew on instances (dhclient -r; dhclient) or restart network agent, and as a short-term measure we added a conservative lease expiry override to reduce the window (30s) for affected subnets.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause is a race in the peering reconciliation code where DHCP option attachments are reconciled using a shared options cache keyed by peering ID. During rapid peering controller failover the cache returned the wrong options set due to stale index pointers; reconciliation code then applied those values to tenant subnet bindings without double-checking tenant ownership. Additionally, client-side DHCP behavior meant the change was applied immediately (via DHCP inform/option update) for certain OSes, causing immediate resolver changes.
fix_summary: 1) Add ownership validation to DHCP option reconciliation so options are only applied when the peering controller confirms tenant affinity. 2) Convert the shared options cache to versioned entries and atomically swap pointers to prevent reading stale sets during controller leader transitions. 3) Add a conservative gating delay (5s) and a verification readback to confirm the applied options match intended tenant values before committing the change. 4) Add an integration test that simulates leader election and ensures no cross-tenant options leak.
deployment_plan: Canary: Deploy to control-plane fleet subset (10% peering controllers) in us-west-2 for 4 hours and monitor DHCP option writes and resolver mismatch metrics.
Observe: track metric 'dhcp.options.apply.failure' and custom metric 'tenant.dhcp.leak.events' in Datadog. Ensure zero leak events in canary window.
Gradual roll: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 24 hours if no regressions. Maintain rollback tag for each stage.
Post-deploy: schedule forced lease refresh job for active tenants that had a migration during maintenance window to minimize client exposure.
testing_notes: Unit: added unit tests for cache versioning and ownership validation (infra/dhcp_cache_test.go).
Integration: new e2e scenario that simulates peering leader election while tenants are active and asserts no DHCP options cross-apply (tests/e2e/peering_dhcp_isolation_test.py).
Customer-sim: ran repro harness against customer tenant snapshot for 3 customers who reported the issue and verified resolution.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alert 'tenant_dhcp_option_write_to_wrong_tenant' created with severity P0. Dashboard added to Console release 'runtime-1.23' showing DHCP option writes by peering-controller instance, tenant_id, and timestamp. Added logscope filter 'dhcp-reconcile' for quick triage. Pager escalation: on >1 event in 10 minutes -> oncall infra -> SE -> Eng SRE.
